item.title: [stayInformed] (Updated) Microsoft Authenticator: Usability improvements for iOS and Android
item.description:
Updated October 29, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

[What and why]

We’re updating Microsoft Authenticator with several usability improvements across iOS and Android. These updates include a refreshed home experience, clearer guidance for accounts that need to be restored, improvements to restoration and sign-in flows, and additional prompts designed to help keep Authenticator working reliably. Availability and timing vary by platform.

[Rollout schedule]

  • General Availability (Worldwide, GCC, GCC High, and DoD): Beginning in early November 2026 (previously October) and expected to complete in late November 2026
  • The improved restoration experience for push notifications and passwordless sign-in will be available on iOS first, with Android planned to follow in January 2027.

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Users of Microsoft Authenticator on iOS and Android

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Authenticator for iOS and Android

What will happen

  • Improved Authenticator home experience, iOS and Android: The Authenticator home page is being updated to improve the experience when users view and manage their accounts. On Android, this update will be available in November 2026.

iOs:

Android:

  • Clearer notification for accounts that haven’t been restored, iOS and Android: Users with accounts that have not yet been restored will see a banner informing them that those accounts require attention

. 

  • Improved first-run guidance for account restoration, iOS and Android: The first-run experience will more clearly show which accounts need to be restored, giving users additional context during Authenticator setup.

  • App rating prompt during sign-in, iOS only: Users may see an option to rate Microsoft Authenticator as part of the sign-in experience, giving them an opportunity to provide feedback about the app. 
  • Improved restoration experience for push notifications and passwordless sign-in: The restoration flow is being improved for users who use push notifications and passwordless sign-in. This improvement will be available on iOS first, with Android planned for January 2027. 
  • Prompt to exclude Authenticator from battery optimization, Android only: After successfully completing an interactive authentication, users may see a non-blocking prompt to exclude Authenticator from Android battery optimization. Excluding the app from battery optimization helps users stay signed in and continue receiving work or school notifications. The prompt will not block authentication.

[Action required and recommendations]

No configuration action is specified in this request.

  • Inform your help desk and security operations teams about the updated Authenticator experiences.
  • Update internal user guidance and screenshots that show the previous Authenticator experiences.

[Compliance considerations]

No compliance considerations identified.

item.title: [stayInformed] (Updated) Microsoft Teams: Initiate side conversations within the meeting chat window
item.description:
Updated October 29, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

[What and Why:]

Microsoft Teams will enable meeting participants to start and continue one-to-one or small-group conversations directly from the meeting chat experience. Users can create a side conversation without leaving the meeting context, helping them coordinate, ask questions, share information, and collaborate in parallel while keeping the main meeting discussion focused.

[Rollout Schedule:]

General Availability (Worldwide, GCC, GCC High, DoD): We will begin rolling out in early December 2026 (previously early January 2027) and expect to complete in mid-January 2027 (previously late January).

[Impact on Your Organization:]

Users will be able to start or continue private 1:1 and group chats directly from the meeting chat experience, without leaving the meeting window. Existing chat history is preserved, so conversations remain part of the user’s regular Teams chat history.

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

No admin action is required. This feature does not introduce a new chat surface, admin policy, or meeting option. Users can turn off the side-chat tab experience if they prefer not to use it.

[Compliance considerations:]

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.

item.title: [planForChange] (Updated) Transitioning Teams Android Device Management from Teams admin Center to the Teams Rooms Pro Management portal
item.description:
Updated October 28, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

[Introduction]

As part of our ongoing mission to deliver a modern, secure, and scalable one-stop management portal for admins, we are transitioning Teams Android device management from the Teams admin center (TAC) to the Teams Rooms Pro Management portal (PMP).

This move consolidates management of all Teams devices, including Teams Rooms on Windows, Teams Rooms on Android, Teams phones, and Teams panels, into a single unified portal, providing IT admins a consistent and seamless experience for managing devices at scale.

This message is associated with Roadmap ID 555235.

[When this will happen:]

  • General Availability (Worldwide): Effective July 2, 2026, the rollout is 100% complete across all regions in the Public cloud. 
  • General Availability (GCC): We expect to start the rollout by Nov 2026 and complete by late-Nov 2026 (previously late-Oct). 
  • General Availability (GCC High and DoD): Effective October 8, 2026, the rollout is 100% complete across GCCH and DoD clouds. 
  • Device management deprecation in TAC: The deprecation of Teams device management capabilities in TAC will begin in November 2026 and will roll out in phases based on device type and feature readiness. 
    • For public clouds - 
      • SIP, MTR-A and Panels devices administration experience in TAC will start deprecating by Mid-November and will complete by end of November. 
      • Phones devices administration experience in TAC will start deprecating by early December and complete by December 15th. 
    • For Gov clouds ( GCC, GCC-H and DoD) 
      • For GCC-H and DoD, device administration experience in TAC will start deprecating by early December and will be completed by December 15th. 
      • For GCC, devices administration experience in TAC will start deprecating by early January and will be completed by January 30th. 
      • Phones devices administration experience for all Sovereign cloud (GCC, GCC-H, DoD) customers will start deprecating by early January and will be completed by January 30th.

[How this affects your organization:]

Who is affected:

Admins who manage Teams Rooms on Android, Teams phones, Teams panels, and SIP Phones.

What will happen:

  • Android device management capabilities, including inventory, updates, health monitoring, and settings will transition from TAC to PMP for the device types, Teams Rooms on Android, Teams phones, Teams panels and SIP Phones.
  • The following capabilities will be available and enhanced in PMP:
    • Device inventories for Android-based Teams Rooms, phones, and panels, including metadata and app information
    • Remote device actions (restart, log collection, sign-in/out, provisioning, and more)
    • Update management
    • Device settings management
    • Device health monitoring
    • SIP device management
  • PMP will become the primary portal for all Teams device management. By January 2027, overlapping TAC capabilities (updates, settings, restart, sign-in/out, log collection, provisioning) will be deprecated in TAC.
  • The article below serves as the main information source for this transition. It has been updated with the latest timelines, milestones, migration guidance, and readiness steps. We will keep updating it as the rollout progresses.
    • Transitioning Teams Android Device Management from Teams Admin Center to the Teams Rooms Pro Management Portal - Microsoft Teams | Microsoft Learn

[What you need to do to prepare:]

  • Monitor the below article for any feature specific updates and timelines. This article also provides migration guidance and pre-requisites for successful transition to PMP.
    • Transitioning Teams Android Device Management from Teams Admin Center to the Teams Rooms Pro Management Portal - Microsoft Teams | Microsoft Learn
  • Learn more about Pro Management portal features with these Teams Rooms Pro Management short YouTube videos.
  • Update internal helpdesk and IT documentation to reference PMP as the new management portal.

[Compliance considerations]

No compliance considerations identified, review as appropriate for your organization.

item.title: [stayInformed] Microsoft Teams: Report guest invitations for security concerns
item.description:
[What and Why:]

Microsoft Teams will enable users to report guest invitations for security concerns directly from Teams. When users receive an unexpected or potentially malicious invitation to join another organization as a guest, they can report it to their IT admin for review, helping identify and mitigate phishing and other abuse through guest invitations.

[Rollout Schedule:]

General Availability (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out in early November 2026 and expect to complete by mid-November 2026.

[Impact on Your Organization:]

Users can report suspicious guest invitations when declining them in Teams. Reports are shared with their IT admin through the User reported security submissions report in the Teams admin center and with Microsoft for review.

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

No action is required for organizations that already have Report a security concern enabled in their Teams messaging policy. Admins can manage this capability through Teams admin center > Messaging policies > Report a security concern.

[Compliance considerations:]

QuestionAnswer
Does the change include an admin control?Yes. The capability is controlled through the Teams messaging policy setting for Report a security concern.

item.title: [planForChange] Microsoft Teams: Impersonation protection for Teams meetings
item.description:
[What and Why:]

Impersonation protection for Teams meetings helps users identify potentially deceptive participants and meeting organizers. When Teams detects a potential impersonation attempt, it surfaces warnings and risk indicators to help users recognize suspicious identities and make more informed decisions when joining or participating in a meeting.

[Rollout Schedule:]

General Availability (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out in mid-December 2026 and expect to complete by late December 2026.

[Impact on Your Organization:]

Meeting Impersonation Protection provides users with additional context to determine whether the people they interact with in Microsoft Teams meetings are who they claim to be. By surfacing warnings and risk indicators when potential impersonation is detected, Teams helps users recognize suspicious identities earlier and make safer decisions.

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

No immediate admin action is required. Admins should familiarize themselves with the new protection experience and communicate the change to users and security teams as appropriate.

[Compliance considerations:]

QuestionAnswer
Does the change introduce or modify security controls?Yes. The feature surfaces meeting impersonation warnings and risk indicators to help users make safer meeting decisions.

item.title: [stayInformed] (Updated) New Outlook for Windows: All Accounts view brings email into a single inbox view
item.description:
Updated October 28, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

[What and Why:]

The All Accounts view, also known as Unified Inbox, lets users see email from multiple connected accounts in a single inbox view in the new Outlook for Windows without merging their mailboxes. Each account's inbox stays separate, and All Accounts view brings messages together so users can triage mail from one place.

Users can read, delete, search, move, archive, and mark messages across accounts without switching between mailboxes. The experience integrates with Copilot for AI-assisted email workflows and supports Search with Copilot for finding messages across the user's primary account.

[Rollout Schedule:]

General Availability (Worldwide): We began rolling out in late September 2026 and expect to complete by late November 2026 (previously late October).

[Impact on Your Organization:]

Users with more than one connected account in the new Outlook for Windows will be able to triage email across accounts from a single All Accounts view. This does not merge mailboxes or move messages between accounts. Each account remains separate, and All Accounts view provides a unified view only.

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

No admin action is required at this time. New admin controls for Unified Inbox are planned for release later in October 2026. Once available, admins will be able to manage whether Unified Inbox is enabled or disabled by default and whether users can change that setting.

We will provide updated documentation and rollout guidance when the admin controls become available.

[Compliance considerations:]

This feature provides a unified view across connected accounts in the new Outlook for Windows but does not merge mailboxes or move messages between accounts. Review your organization's Outlook account and automated-assistance policies as appropriate.

item.title: [stayInformed] Microsoft 365 admin center: Pin Microsoft Copilot app setting for users with a paid Microsoft 365 Copilot license
item.description:
[What and Why:]

We are updating the Pin Microsoft Copilot app to the Windows taskbar setting in the Microsoft 365 admin center based on customer feedback, giving administrators more flexibility and clarity when managing Copilot taskbar pinning. This update introduces two changes:

  1. New option to pin for users with a paid Microsoft 365 Copilot license: Admins will be able to target taskbar pinning to users with a paid Microsoft 365 Copilot license.
  2. "Do not pin" will no longer be preselected by default: When no pinning preference has been explicitly saved, the setting will open with no option selected. This changes only what the admin center displays. It does not change how the app is pinned on any device.

[Rollout Schedule:]

  • General Availability (Worldwide): Rollout will begin in early December 2026 and is expected to complete by mid-December 2026.

[Impact on Your Organization:]

Who is affected

  • Administrators who manage Microsoft Copilot taskbar pinning.
  • Organizations that use this setting, including those that want to target taskbar pinning to users with a paid Microsoft 365 Copilot license.

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft 365 admin center
  • Microsoft Entra
  • Microsoft Intune
  • Microsoft Copilot app for Windows

What will happen

  • The setting is available in Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Settings > Pin Microsoft Copilot app to the Windows taskbar.
  • A new Pin for users with a paid Microsoft 365 Copilot license option will be available. When an admin selects and saves this option, the Microsoft 365 admin center will create a license-based group in Microsoft Entra on the admin's behalf and use the existing Intune policy flow to target eligible users.
  • To target pinning to a custom mix of user segments in your tenant, you can use the existing Pin for selected groups option in addition to the new option.
  • When an admin has not configured the setting, Do not pin for anyone will no longer be preselected. After this update, no option will be preselected until an admin makes an explicit choice.
  • If your organization has not previously configured this setting, no action is needed. To enable pinning, select and save a pinning option.
  • If you previously saved Do not pin, no new pins will be added, but the setting will appear with no option selected after the update. To have the admin center explicitly record and display Do not pin, select and save it again.
  • If you previously saved Pin for all devices or Pin for selected groups, no action is needed. Your existing selection will be preserved, and pinning will continue according to that configuration. You can select the new option if it better fits your organization's needs.
  • In all cases, Do not pin only stops new pins from being added through this setting. It does not remove pins that already exist.

Pin for all users with a paid Copilot license

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

We recommend that you review your organization's preferred Microsoft Copilot taskbar pinning configuration.

If you plan to use the paid-license targeting option, ensure that the administrator configuring the setting has permission to create security groups in Microsoft Entra. If the administrator does not have this permission, the setting cannot create the required license-based group, and the change will not be saved.

Your organization's existing permissions and eligibility requirements for managing Microsoft Copilot taskbar pinning continue to apply. After the update is available:

  1. Go to Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Settings > View all.
  2. Select Pin Microsoft Copilot app to the Windows taskbar.
  3. Review the available pinning options.
  4. Choose the option that fits your organization. To pin the app only for users with paid Microsoft 365 Copilot licenses, select Pin for users with a paid Microsoft 365 Copilot license.
  5. Select Save.

[Learn more]

  • Pin Microsoft Copilot to the Windows taskbar | Microsoft Learn
  • Understand and manage dynamic group processing in Microsoft Entra ID - Microsoft Entra ID | Microsoft Learn

[Compliance considerations:]

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.

item.title: [stayInformed] Office in Copilot brings the full power of Office into the Microsoft Copilot app
item.description:
[What and Why:]

Now users have the full power of Office in Microsoft Copilot app, so users can create, edit and collaborate on Word, Excel and PowerPoint files, without leaving the app.

[Rollout Schedule:]

General Availability (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out in mid-November 2026 and expect to complete by mid-November 2026.

[Impact on Your Organization:]

Now with the full value of Office in Copilot,  Word, Excel, and PowerPoint is brought in directly into the Copilot experience, allowing users to create, review, edit, and collaborate on Office files without leaving their flow of work. This reduces context switching and makes it easier to move from an idea or conversation to a finished, shareable Office artifact.

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

No admin action is required. Admins may want to inform users about the new experience and review their existing Microsoft 365 Copilot configuration and policies.

[Compliance considerations:]

QuestionAnswer
Does the change alter how existing customer data is processed, stored, or accessed?Yes. Users can now access and edit Office file content through the Copilot experience, with changes synced back to the regular Office apps.
Does the change introduce or significantly modify AI/ML or agent capabilities that interact with or provide access to customer data?Yes. Copilot gains expanded capability to read and edit Office document content as part of this feature.
Does the change provide end users any new way of interacting with generative AI?Yes. Users can create and edit Word, Excel, and PowerPoint content directly within the Copilot app.
Does the change include an admin control and can it be controlled through Entra ID group membership?Yes. This feature is subject to existing Microsoft 365 Copilot configuration and policies, which admins can manage via Entra ID group-based assignment.

item.title: [planForChange] Power Platform – Information about the 2026 time zone changes in Canada
item.description:
What and why
Power Platform services are being updated to support the 2026 time zone changes in Manitoba, Alberta, and British Columbia. This is a general awareness message to support the changes and complements MC1510951 — Windows updates are available for 2026 time zone changes in Canada.

Rollout schedule
Updates will be delivered by service to support the November 1, 2026, time zone transition. Availability will vary by service.

Power Automate Desktop (RPA): Scheduled trigger updates are planned to roll out November 5 through November 23, 2026.

How does this affect me?
Impact varies by component and time zone configuration:
  • Power Apps (Model-driven Apps): Selecting a new regional time zone may change how existing dates and times are displayed where the old and new rules differ.
  • Power Apps (Canvas Apps): Date and time behavior depends on the device’s time zone configuration. Affected users may see incorrect local times if their device has not been updated and configured with the correct regional time zone.
  • Power Pages: From November 1, 2026, through December 31, 2026, dates converted by Dataverse and date-based filters may be one hour behind. From 2027, dates and times recorded during past standard-time periods may also display one hour incorrectly. Dates rendered directly in the browser are not affected by the identified issue.
  • Power Automate Process Mining: Date and time behavior depends on the device’s time zone configuration. Affected users may see incorrect local times if their device has not been updated and configured with the correct regional time zone.
  • Power Automate Desktop (RPA): Beginning November 1, scheduled triggers using the existing Mountain, Pacific, or Central time zones may run one hour off from the intended local time in affected regions. The Get current date and time action also has limitations involving unavailable new time zone options and outdated time zone data.
What action do I need to take?
Keep device operating systems and browsers updated and verify that each device uses the correct regional time zone as time zone settings may not change automatically.

After the relevant service update is available, affected users should select the appropriate new region-specific time zone in their app or service settings, where applicable.

Power Automate Desktop (RPA): Install the October 2026 Windows time zone update on machines running desktop flows. Until the new regional time zones are available for scheduled triggers, use these temporary settings:
  • Alberta: Select “Saskatchewan.”
  • British Columbia: Select “Arizona.”
  • Manitoba: Select “Bogota, Lima, Quito.”

item.title: [stayInformed] Engage plugin for Copilot Cowork and Autopilot: General availability
item.description:
[What and Why:]

We are introducing the Engage plugin for Copilot Cowork and Autopilot, with general availability targeted for November 16, 2026.

The plugin brings Engage conversations and actions into Copilot workflows. Users can catch up on community discussions, find relevant information, understand employee questions and feedback, and draft or publish updates without switching to Engage.

[Rollout Schedule:]

General Availability (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out in mid-November 2026 and expect to complete by mid-November 2026.

[Impact on Your Organization:]

Users can bring Engage into workflows alongside information from other connected sources. For example, they can use recent meetings and Teams discussions to prepare an update and publish it to an Engage community.

The plugin supports finding and summarizing conversations, reviewing replies and reactions, creating posts, replying to discussions, and adding reactions. It operates using the signed-in user’s existing Engage permissions and does not grant additional access to content or actions.

The plugin is off by default. Administrators control its availability to their organization or selected users and groups.

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

No action is required unless you want to make it available to your organization.

Consider updating your helpdesk and internal user guidance if you plan to enable the plugin.

  • Administrators should review Manage plugins for Copilot Cowork for licensing requirements, deployment options, and access controls.
  • For user setup and usage instructions, see Use plugins with Copilot Cowork.

[Compliance considerations:]

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.

item.title: [stayInformed] Microsoft Copilot Feedback UX update
item.description:
[What and Why:]

We’re updating the thumbs-down feedback experience in Microsoft Copilot to make it easier for users to provide specific, actionable feedback. Today, many thumbs-down responses are submitted without comments, providing sentiment but limited information about the issue. When users select thumbs down, they’ll be able to select one or more feedback categories and optionally provide additional comments, giving each categorized response a signal that can be routed to the appropriate team or issue type.

[Rollout Schedule:]

General Availability (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out in late October 2026 and expect to complete by late October 2026.

[Impact on Your Organization:]

Users who can submit feedback in supported Microsoft Copilot experiences may see the updated thumbs-down feedback form. The planned audience includes users signed in with Microsoft Entra ID organizational accounts, users signed in with consumer Microsoft accounts, and users in Education tenants. The feature isn’t currently planned for Mobile, GCC, GCC High, DoD, or other sovereign cloud environments.

The updated feedback experience is planned for Microsoft Copilot, Copilot in Microsoft Edge, Copilot in Microsoft Outlook, and Copilot in Microsoft Teams, across web browsers, Windows, and macOS. The WXPN/Catalyst experience isn’t currently included.

When a user selects thumbs down on a Copilot response, they may see selectable categories describing the issue, can select more than one category, and can optionally enter additional feedback in a free-text field. The thumbs-up feedback experience isn’t changing. This update applies only to the existing “Allow users to submit feedback to Microsoft” admin policy; all other feedback policy experiences remain unchanged. During the controlled rollout, some users will continue to see the existing feedback experience.

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

No admin action is required for this change. It will be visible to users who are already allowed to submit feedback under the existing policy.

[Compliance considerations:]

QuestionAnswer
Does the change store new customer data?Yes. When a user chooses to submit thumbs-down feedback, the selected categories, optional free-text comment, and optional screenshot are new data captured as part of that submission.
Does the change include an admin control and can it be controlled through Entra ID group membership?Yes. This UX change applies to the existing "Allow users to submit feedback to Microsoft" admin policy; all other feedback policy experiences remain unchanged.

item.title: [stayInformed] (Updated) Microsoft Teams: External presenter support for event group chat
item.description:
Updated October 29, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

[What and why]

We are adding support for external presenters in event group chat, the private chat used by organizers, co-organizers, and presenters for coordination during an event or structured meeting. This change enables presenters who are outside the tenant hosting the meeting or event to participate in the event group chat.

[Rollout schedule]

  • General Availability (Worldwide): Rollout will begin in early December 2026 (previously early November) and is expected to complete by early January 2027 (previously early December 2026).

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Organizers, co-organizers, and presenters using event group chat in meetings or events, including external presenters.

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Teams
  • Event group chat
  • Meetings and events with the Enable Green room Teams meeting option enabled

What will happen

  • External presenters will be able to join the event group chat used for coordination during a meeting or event.
  • The meeting or event must have the Enable Green room Teams meeting option enabled to use event group chat. 
  • External user collaboration must be enabled for external presenters to use this functionality.

[Action required and recommendations]

If your organization wants external presenters to use event group chat, ensure external user collaboration is enabled in Teams admin center > External collaboration.

[Compliance considerations]

Does the change store new customer data?

  • No. Expected changes on the client will only correct the tenantId to the external federated presenter's own tenant.

Does the change alter how existing customer data is processed, stored, or accessed (e.g., documents, emails, chats, etc.)?

  • Yes. External federated presenters can now read and post in the event group chat. That includes messages written before they joined, if the thread shows history. The presenter's stored tenantId also changes from the organizer's tenant to the presenter's own tenant.

Does the change provide a new way of communicating between users, tenants, or subscriptions?

  • Yes. We are adding a new cross-tenant chat path between the organizer's tenant and external presenters. Both tenants must allow external access.

Does the change modify how users can access, export, delete, or correct their personal data within Microsoft 365 services (GDPR Data Subject Rights)?

  • No. External presenters' messages fall under existing federated-chat handling.

item.title: [preventOrFixIssue] Microsoft Entra ID: Risk-based anti-bot verification (CAPTCHA) for SMS and voice authentication
item.description:
Updated October 26, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

[What and why]

Microsoft Entra ID is adding safeguards to reduce automated abuse of telephony-based authentication. SMS and voice authentication options are not being removed. Some users who use SMS or voice for first-factor sign-in may be asked to complete a risk-based anti-bot verification step (CAPTCHA) before a code is sent.

[Rollout schedule]

  • Rollout began in mid-October 2026 and is ongoing. 
  • Users may see an anti-bot verification step for first-factor telephony-based authentications.

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Some users who use SMS or voice as a first-factor sign-in method

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Entra ID telephony-based authentication using SMS or voice for first-factor sign-in

What will happen

  • Some users might see an additional risk-based anti-bot verification step (CAPTCHA) before Microsoft sends the telephony code.
  • The experience is determined based on client behaviors, so not every user or sign-in attempt will be affected.
  • If the verification experience does not load because of restrictive network or firewall settings, affected users might not be able to complete the flow until required endpoints are allowed. Endpoint guidance is included in the linked documentation below.

[Action required and recommendations]

  • Prepare your help desk and user communications for the possibility of an anti-bot verification step before a telephony code is sent.
  • Review the linked documentation for network-readiness guidance, including any approved endpoint or allowlist requirements.
  • Continue moving users to phishing-resistant authentication methods, such as passkeys, where possible.

Learn more 

  • Understanding telephony fraud risk for Microsoft Entra multifactor authentication - Microsoft Entra ID | Microsoft Learn
  • Risk-based anti-bot verification (CAPTCHA) for telephony-based sign-in - Microsoft Entra ID | Microsoft Learn
  • Passkeys by default and retirement of Microsoft-provided SMS and voice authentication - Microsoft Entra ID | Microsoft Learn

[Compliance considerations]

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.

item.title: [stayInformed] Microsoft Copilot Studio cost controls are expanding to Cost Management in the Microsoft 365 admin center
item.description:
We are announcing the ability to use the expanded cost controls for Cost Management for Copilot Studio into the Microsoft 365 admin center in Power Platform. This feature will reach general availability by November 20, 2026.

How does this affect me?
This update gives administrators a centralized way to manage Copilot Credit spending across supported usage-based AI workloads while retaining broader Copilot Studio administration in the Power Platform admin center. This enterprise-ready management experience helps organizations monitor usage and apply spending controls that align with their operational and budget requirements. This will be available for:
  • AI administrators and global administrators who manage costs in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
  • Power Platform administrators who manage Copilot Studio environments in the Power Platform admin center.
  • Billing and cost administrators who monitor Copilot Credit usage and spending.
When this change is available:
  • Administrators will be able to manage spending for supported Copilot Studio resources by using Cost Management spending policies in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
  • Spending policies can be applied to a supported environment or an individual agent. Administrators can also choose to apply a policy across supported environments.
  • This experience is not enabled automatically for existing Copilot Studio environments. Moving cost-policy management is optional and is controlled by an administrator for each environment.
  • For an environment moved to the new experience, the Microsoft 365 admin center spending policy becomes the active cost control.
  • After an environment is moved, new usage information for that environment will appear in the Microsoft 365 admin center and will no longer appear in the Power Platform admin center.
  • Usage information generated before the environment was moved will remain available in the Power Platform admin center.
  • Environments that are not moved will continue to use their existing cost controls in the Power Platform admin center.
  • Other Copilot Studio administration will remain in the Power Platform admin center. Only cost-policy management and associated reporting for moved environments will change.

item.title: [stayInformed] Frontier expands to include public previews in Microsoft Teams, new Outlook for Windows, OneDrive, and SharePoint

[What and Why:]

Frontier now covers more of Microsoft 365. Starting in November 2026, users enrolled in Frontier will start getting eligible public preview features in Microsoft Teams, new Outlook for Windows, OneDrive, and SharePoint, in addition to Copilot.

Instead of looking in different places for previews, admins use one program and one setting to give the users they choose early access across Microsoft 365.

Frontier is optional and controlled by your admins. It is separate from each user's Standard release or Deferred release preference, which still decides when users receive features once they're generally available. If you already have users enrolled in Frontier, they don't need to re-enroll.

Release options in the Microsoft 365 admin center:

  • Frontier (preview access): Opt in specific users and groups, or all users, to get eligible public preview features before general availability.
  • Standard release (general availability): Receive updates as soon as they're generally available. This is the default.

[Rollout Schedule:]

[Impact on Your Organization:]

Frontier makes early access to Microsoft 365 previews simpler and more predictable. Instead of looking in different places for previews, your organization gets eligible public preview features for Microsoft Teams, new Outlook for Windows, OneDrive, SharePoint, and Copilot through one program, managed from one admin setting. Admins choose which users and groups take part, and everyone else stays on their Standard release or Deferred release schedule, so it's clear who gets what and when. 

In November 2026, admins can also manage Frontier, Standard release, and Deferred release together in one place in the Microsoft 365 admin center. Early access gives you time to prepare guidance and support teams, and a way to share feedback before features are broadly released.

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

item.title: [planForChange] Microsoft Windows: Updates to address compromised eMudhra certificate authority keys
item.description:
[What and why]

Microsoft is responding to an issue involving eight eMudhra intermediate certificate authority (CA) private keys, six associated with TLS and two with code signing. Because these keys could be recovered, they could potentially be used to create certificates or sign content that appeared to come from a trusted CA. The issue arose in eMudhra's certificate hierarchy and was not a compromise of Microsoft systems.

Microsoft is updating certificate trust to block affected certificate authorities and remove certificates associated with the affected hierarchies.

[Rollout schedule]

  • General Availability (Worldwide, GCC, GCC High, DoD): Beginning in late October 2026 and expected to complete by late October 2026

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Organizations using Windows, Microsoft Edge, or WebView2, particularly organizations with certificates that chain to one of the eight certificates being removed
  • Organizations managing disconnected Windows devices or disconnected Azure devices may need to take additional action

Platforms and services

  • Windows
  • Microsoft Edge
  • WebView2
  • Azure virtual machines

What will happen

  • Microsoft has published an update to the Windows Disallowed Certificate Trust List to block the affected certificate authorities.
  • Microsoft has deployed a separate CRLSet update for Microsoft Edge and WebView2 to block affected TLS certificates signed by the affected certificate authorities.
  • The Microsoft Edge and WebView2 update is delivered automatically through the component update mechanism. Customers do not need to install a new browser version.
  • Microsoft has released updates to Windows and Microsoft Edge to remove certificates associated with the affected hierarchies from their trust lists.
  • After these updates reach a device, the affected certificates will no longer be trusted by default through the respective trust lists.

[Action required and recommendations]

  • Keep updates flowing. Allow automatic Windows certificate trust updates and Microsoft Edge component updates to reach your devices.
  • Check disconnected Windows devices. If you manage Windows devices that do not receive automatic updates, make sure your update process delivers the updated Disallowed Certificate Trust List and upcoming trust-list changes. See the Microsoft Learn guidance in Learn more for information about distributing certificate trust lists in disconnected environments.
  • Review disconnected Azure devices. Review disconnected Azure devices running on Virtual Machine Scale Sets (VMSS) or single-instance VMs. Updated images are available in Azure Marketplace, and customers can deploy them to protect against this vulnerability.
  • Replace dependent certificates. If any of your certificates chain to one of the seven certificates being removed, identify those dependencies and obtain replacement certificates or an alternative trusted chain before the changes reach your devices.

Learn more

  • Microsoft’s response to compromised eMudhra certificate authority keys
  • Configure trusted roots and disallowed certificates in Windows | Microsoft Learn

[Compliance considerations]

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.

item.title: [planForChange] (Updated) Microsoft Entra: Windows Hello for Business and macOS Platform SSO as standalone MFA factors
item.description:
Updated October 27, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

[What and why]

Microsoft Entra will soon recognize Windows Hello for Business (WHfB) and macOS Platform Single Sign-On (PSSO) as standalone multifactor authentication (MFA) factors in supported authentication scenarios.

Today, WHfB and macOS PSSO can satisfy MFA requirements during primary sign-in, but users may still be required to register and use an additional passkey or authentication method for certain step-up authentication prompts, Authentication Strength policies, and sign-in frequency checks.

After this rollout, users who authenticate with WHfB or macOS PSSO will be able to satisfy supported MFA requirements without registering an additional passkey. This change helps organizations expand the use of phishing-resistant authentication methods and reduce reliance on less secure authentication methods. As part of this change, a user's WHfB and macOS PSSO credentials will be displayed in My Security Info as auto-registered passkeys.

[Rollout schedule]

  • General Availability (Worldwide, GCC): Beginning in early November 2026 (previously early October) and expected to complete in late December 2026 (previously mid-December)

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Organizations using Microsoft Entra ID
  • Users who authenticate with Windows Hello for Business
  • Users who authenticate with macOS Platform SSO
  • Organizations using Conditional Access Authentication Strength policies

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Entra ID
  • Windows Hello for Business
  • macOS Platform SSO
  • Conditional Access
  • Authentication Strength policies

What will happen

After rollout:

  • Users signing in with WHfB or macOS PSSO can complete supported MFA challenges without requiring a separate passkey.
  • WHfB and macOS PSSO will satisfy supported MFA requirements for step-up authentication scenarios.
  • WHfB and macOS PSSO can be used during 2FA to satisfy supported Authentication Strength policy requirements.
  • WHfB and macOS PSSO can be used during 2FA to satisfy supported sign-in frequency challenge requirements.
  • Users whose only MFA method is WHfB or macOS PSSO will be considered MFA-capable.
  • Users who sign in with only a password will no longer be automatically prompted to register an additional MFA method if WHfB or macOS PSSO is their only registered MFA credential.
  • Users with WHfB or macOS PSSO credentials, will be able to see them listed in My Security Info as auto-registered passkeys.

[Action required and recommendations]

No configuration changes are required.

We recommend reviewing user onboarding and MFA registration processes before rollout. Because WHfB and macOS PSSO credentials are device-bound, users may not be able to complete MFA challenges from devices where those credentials are not available.

Recommended actions:

  • Update onboarding guidance to ensure users register at least one portable MFA method.
  • Consider requiring users to register a synced passkey or Microsoft Authenticator passkey in addition to WHfB or macOS PSSO.
  • Review custom Authentication Strength policies to confirm WHfB and macOS PSSO are allowed where appropriate.
  • Update user documentation because users with only WHfB or macOS PSSO registered will no longer be automatically guided to register an additional MFA method.

Learn more (To be updated closer to GA rollout.)

item.title: [stayInformed] (Updated) OneDrive for Business: Improved Windows Desktop sync error messages for max path length

[What and why]

We are improving the OneDrive sync experience on Windows desktop to provide clearer, more actionable guidance when file and folder paths exceed the supported 520-character limit. The updated experience will show exactly how many characters a path exceeds the limit and will provide a guided flow to rename or move affected items so they can sync successfully.

This improvement addresses a common OneDrive sync issue by reducing user confusion, minimizing workflow disruption, and helping users resolve errors faster.

This update is associated with Microsoft 365 Roadmap ID 557563.

[Rollout schedule]

General Availability (Worldwide): Beginning January 2027 (previously end of October 2026) and expected to complete by end of January 2027 (previously end of November 2026)

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • All users of the OneDrive sync client on Windows desktop

Platforms and services

  • OneDrive for Business (Windows desktop sync client)

What will happen

Max path errors are one of the most commonly reported issues by OneDrive sync users. Currently, when a file or folder path exceeds the 520-character sync limit, the error message only states how many characters the path exceeds the limit and asks users to shorten it. In addition, File Explorer limitations may prevent users from renaming paths over 260 characters, and the sync client may stop syncing until the issue is resolved.

As part of this improved error experience, when users encounter max path errors, the sync client will continue running and users will be guided through a custom rename and move experience.

With this update:

  • The sync client will continue running when users encounter max path errors
  • Users will be guided through a custom rename and move experience to resolve issues directly

The rename experience will:

  • Show the number of over-limit characters
  • Highlight which items in the path can be renamed
  • Allow renames even when the path exceeds 260 characters

Screenshot - Custom rename dialog

The move experience will:

  • Show over-limit character counts in a guided interface
  • Display warning dialogs for over-limit shared items in OneDrive
  • Display warning dialogs for over-limit items in shortcuts

Screenshot - Example warning dialog for overlimit items in shortcuts

These enhancements are designed to reduce troubleshooting time and improve the overall sync experience.

[Action required and recommendations]

No admin action is required. This update will be automatically available through the OneDrive sync client.

You may want to:

  • Inform your helpdesk and support teams about the improved error messages, as this update should reduce max-path-related support tickets.

item.title: [preventOrFixIssue] (Updated) Windows updates are available for 2026 time zone changes in Canada
item.description:
(Updated October 16, 2026: Added guidance for managing the Alberta and British Columbia time zone changes in Outlook Time Zone Changes for Alberta and British Columbia.)

(Updated October 27, 2026: Included reference and link to more guidance published in the Message center post MC1526468.)

[What and why:]

Windows updates are now available to support the 2026 time zone changes in Manitoba, Alberta, and British Columbia. On November 1, 2026, clocks in affected regions will not be set back by one hour.

Manitoba will permanently stay on UTC-5, Alberta and affected locations will permanently stay on UTC-6, and most of British Columbia will permanently stay on UTC-7. The new Windows updates add region-specific time zones to support these changes.

[Rollout schedule:]

  • September 22, 2026: The Alberta and British Columbia changes became available in the September 2026 non-security preview update for Windows 11, versions 25H2 and 24H2.
  • October 13, 2026: The Manitoba change became available for all supported versions of Windows. The Alberta and British Columbia changes became available for all other supported versions of Windows, including Windows Server. These changes are included in the October 2026 security update.
  • November 1, 2026: The time zone transitions take effect at 2:00 a.m. local time. Clocks in affected areas will not be set back by one hour.

[Impact on your organization:]

Devices in affected regions will display an incorrect local time after the November 1, 2026 transition if the applicable Windows update is not installed or the appropriate time zone is not selected. The updates add the following region-specific time zones:

  • (UTC-05:00) Manitoba
  • (UTC-06:00) Mountain Time (Alberta)
  • (UTC-07:00) Pacific Time (British Columbia)

The Alberta time zone change also applies to Yellowknife and Inuvik in the Northwest Territories and locations in southeastern British Columbia that align with Alberta.

Devices configured to set the time zone automatically will select the appropriate new time zone. On other devices, the new region-specific time zone must be selected manually.

[Action required/recommendations:]

  • Install the applicable Windows update on affected devices before November 1, 2026.
  • Confirm that affected devices use the appropriate region-specific time zone after installing the update.
  • If a device cannot receive the update before November 1, 2026, read and follow the interim guidance for each affected region detailed in the Daylight Saving Time & Time Zone Blog and move the device to the appropriate region-specific time zone as soon as possible.

Note: To manage this change in Outlook, please follow the guidance in the article Outlook Time Zone Changes for Alberta and British Columbia. For guidance on how to manage Outlook and Exchange Online calendar events, Microsoft Teams Rooms on Windows, and other potentially impacted Microsoft 365 experiences, see MC1526468.

[Compliance considerations:]

No compliance considerations are identified. Review as appropriate for your organization and region-specific time zone.

item.title: [stayInformed] (Updated) Microsoft 365 Copilot: Use Microsoft Agent 365 agents as connected agents in declarative agents

This enhancement expands the types of external agent services that declarative agents can connect to. In addition to existing support for OpenAPI and Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, declarative agents can now connect to Agent2Agent-enabled agents, enabling natural language interactions and support for more complex workflows.

This feature gives developers greater flexibility when building declarative agents while providing administrators centralized management and governance through the Microsoft 365 admin center.

  • Microsoft 365 admin center
  • Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit
  • Declarative agents

  • Administrators can install Microsoft Agent 365 agents that support the Agent2Agent protocol from the All agents page in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
  • Declarative agents can use approved Agent2Agent-enabled agents as connected agents.
  • Agent2Agent support is added alongside existing support for OpenAPI and MCP server connections.
  • Users cannot install Agent2Agent-enabled Microsoft Agent 365 agents themselves.
  • Administrators can review Agent2Agent-connected agents from the Connected agents tab in the declarative agent details page before approving their use.

item.title: [stayInformed] Change Optics Report
item.description:
[What and Why:]

Following the public preview announced in MC1301802, the Change Optics report for Exchange Online is now generally available for worldwide tenants. The report helps Exchange administrators identify email traffic that may be affected by upcoming service changes so they can investigate and remediate potential issues before enforcement occurs.

Learn more: The Change Optics report is now generally available in Exchange Online

[Rollout Schedule:]

General Availability (Worldwide): The report is available now.

[Impact on Your Organization:]

The Change Optics report is available in the Exchange Admin Center under Reports > Mail flow > Change Optics Report. The report displays a sample set of messages matching characteristics expected to be affected by Exchange Online transport changes. At GA, the report includes:

  • OMC (Onmicrosoft.com external traffic): Identifies onmicrosoft.com traffic sent externally so organizations can investigate and reduce usage affected by onmicrosoft.com throttling.
  • DRS (Direct Send traffic): Identifies Direct Send traffic received by your tenant, helping administrators identify legitimate senders before enabling Reject Direct Send.

Since Public Preview, we've made improvements to the report thanks to the feedback received.

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

No action is required. Exchange administrators may want to:

  • Review the Change Optics Report when future Message Center communications reference a Change Optics scenario.
  • Use the OMC scenario to identify and reduce onmicrosoft.com external email usage.
  • Use the DRS scenario to identify Direct Send traffic and prepare for enabling Reject Direct Send where appropriate.
  • Update internal mail flow operational guidance to incorporate Change Optics as part of change preparation.

item.title: [stayInformed] (Updated) Outlook: Change the organizer of meetings
item.description:
Updated October 26, 2026: We have updated the content and timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

[What and Why:]

Microsoft is introducing Change organizer for eligible Outlook meetings and recurring meeting series. Users can ask another person in their organization to become the organizer, and the selected person must accept before ownership changes. This supports personal and team productivity by maintaining meeting continuity during role changes, leave, and offboarding.

[Rollout Schedule:]

This phase supports non-online meetings:

  • Worldwide: Early November through early December 2026 
  • GCC: Late November through late December 2026 
  • GCC High: Early December through late December 2026 
  • DoD: Early December through late December 2026 

Phase 2 will add eligible online meetings. For Teams meetings, the transfer will generate a new Teams meeting link owned by the new organizer. Phase 2 will also be rolled out along with phase 1 with the same schedule. 

Phase 3 will add transfer support for eligible Teams meeting artifacts, including chat, meeting options, transcripts, recordings, agenda, notes, and attendance reports. Its timing will be announced separately.

[Impact on Your Organization:]

Who is affected:

  1. Users who organize eligible meetings or recurring series.
  2. Users selected to become a new organizer.
  3. Delegates with permission to edit meetings on another user's primary calendar.
  4. Help desk teams supporting meeting ownership transitions.

Platforms/Services:

  1. Outlook on the web
  2. New Outlook for Windows
  3. Teams Microsoft 365 Calendar
  4. Exchange Online

Classic Outlook for Windows is not supported.

What will happen:

  1. The current organizer can select one person in the same organization or tenant and send an organizer change request.
  2. The meeting remains with the current organizer until the selected person accepts.
  3. The organizer or an authorized delegate can cancel a pending request.
  4. For recurring series, future instances move to the new organizer's calendar. Earlier instances remain with the previous organizer.
  5. Internal Exchange Online attendees receive a silent update and do not need to respond again. Their Reminder, Category, Show As, and Private settings are preserved.
  6. External and on-premises attendees receive a cancellation and a new invitation, which requires a response.
  7. The meeting body, attachments, and sensitivity labels are preserved. The new organizer might require separate access to OneDrive attachments or links.
  8. If the meeting has a Teams meeting, a new Teams meeting link will be generated upon transfer which will be owned by the new organizer.
  9. This feature is enabled by default and requires no tenant configuration. There is no admin setting to control the availability of this feature.

The meeting must be in the future, use a work or school account, and be stored on the organizer's primary calendar. Draft, canceled, encrypted, group calendar, group mailbox, and shared mailbox meetings are not eligible.

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

No administrative action is required.

  1. Review meeting ownership processes for role changes, leave, and offboarding.
  2. Update internal meeting management and offboarding documentation.
  3. Tell users that the new organizer must accept the request and that the previous organizer is not automatically retained as an attendee.
  4. Advise users that external attendees must respond to a replacement invitation.
  5. Ask users to confirm that the new organizer can access linked OneDrive content.
  6. Review the Microsoft Support article, Change the organizer of a meeting in Outlook.

[Compliance Considerations:]

ConsiderationImpactExplanation
Does the change alter how existing customer data is processed, stored, or accessed?YesFuture meeting instances move to the new organizer's calendar and can be managed by that organizer. Earlier recurring instances remain with the previous organizer. Meeting content is preserved, but linked OneDrive content might require separate access.
Does the change provide a new way of communicating between users, tenants, or subscriptions?YesThe feature adds organizer transfer requests within an organization. Internal attendees receive silent updates, while external and on-premises attendees receive a cancellation and replacement invitation.

item.title: [planForChange] AI Builder credits retirement: Prepare to use Copilot Credits
item.description:
[What and Why:]

Microsoft is retiring AI Builder credits and replacing them with Copilot Credits. Organizations using AI Builder must arrange Copilot Credit capacity before their existing AI Builder credit entitlements expire, or sooner if those credits are exhausted, to avoid interruptions.

 AI Builder features are not being retired. They will continue to be supported using Copilot Credits, bringing AI Builder and Microsoft Copilot Studio capabilities onto a common credit-based licensing model.

When this will happen:

  • November 1, 2025: Sales of AI Builder capacity add-ons ended for new customers.
  • November 1, 2026: AI Builder capacity add-ons reach end of life. Credits from active add-on contracts remain usable until those contracts expire.
  • November 1, 2026: New or renewed eligible Power Platform and Dynamics 365 licenses will no longer include seeded AI Builder credits. Seeded credits included with eligible licenses purchased or renewed before this date remain available through the end of the applicable contract term.

November 1, 2026, is not a universal cutoff for existing credits. Your transition deadline depends on when your applicable contracts expire.

[Rollout Schedule:]

General Availability (Worldwide, GCC): We will begin rolling out on early November 2026 and expect to complete by early November 2026.

[Impact on Your Organization:]

This change affects organizations that use AI Builder credits from capacity add-ons or credits included with eligible Power Platform and Dynamics 365 licenses to run AI Builder features in Power Apps and Power Automate.

  • AI Builder features in Power Apps and Power Automate consume available AI Builder credits first. When those credits are unavailable or exhausted, usage automatically falls back to available Copilot Credits.
  • If neither credit type is available, affected AI Builder runs are blocked, which can interrupt apps, flows, and business processes.
  • AI Builder credits will not automatically convert to Copilot Credits. Consumption rates differ by capability; there is no single conversion ratio.
  • AI Builder features in Copilot Studio already consume Copilot Credits.
  • This change affects licensing, not feature availability. Administrators must ensure sufficient capacity to continue running AI Builder features.

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

Admin action is required before November 1, 2026, for organizations with AI Builder capacity add-ons, and before existing credit entitlements expire to prevent disruption.

  1. Review your contracts. Identify when your AI Builder capacity add-ons and licenses providing seeded credits expire. For AI Builder capacity add-ons, turn off automatic renewal in the Microsoft 365 admin center or work with your partner to do so in Partner Center.
  2. Review credit consumption across environments. In the Power Platform admin center, go to Licensing > Capacity add-ons > Download reports > + New > AI Builder. Generate and download the report to review credits consumed by date, user, and environment during the 30 days preceding the selected target date.
  3.  3.** Identify affected workloads.** In the Power Automate portal, select the environment, then go to Automation Center > Monitor > AI Builder activity. Makers can review their own activity for models they can access; users with the System Administrator or System Customizer role can review all activity in the environment. Activity data is also available in the AI Event table in Dataverse.
  4. Plan replacement capacity. Use the AI Builder capability rate table to estimate Copilot Credit requirements. Purchase and make sufficient Copilot Credits available to affected environments before existing AI Builder credit entitlements expire. Do not assume that the same number of Copilot Credits will cover your current AI Builder credit usage.
  5. Notify makers and support teams. Update internal licensing guidance and identify business-critical apps and flows that could be interrupted by insufficient capacity.

  • AI Builder licensing overview
  • AI Builder consumption report
  • Monitor AI Builder activity

[Compliance considerations:]

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.
